function: Joint DRL control of drone caching placement, trajectory (speed and angle) and per-user transmit power to minimize average content downloading delay under finite-blocklength URLLC (p. 6).
system: Drone aerial BS at 200 m, K=10 ground users, orthogonal links, backhaul to ground BS; antenna count not given (scalar SNR); no RIS; 2 GHz carrier (pp. 3, 9).
method: Dual-clip PPO deep reinforcement learning (DC-PPO), fully connected actor and critic networks with [256, 128] hidden neurons, trained by interaction with the simulated environment (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: probabilistic LoS/NLoS air-to-ground path loss (Eqs. 8-13) with Gaussian-Markov user mobility and Zipf content requests; no 3GPP model, public dataset or measurements (pp. 4-5, 9).
test_conditions: Trained in the simulated environment (K=10, F=20); delay reported for sweeps of cache size, users, contents, power, blocklength and BER; retraining per setting not stated (pp. 9-13).
baselines: Learned: PPO, A2C, DDPG (p. 9). Random-caching and fixed-trajectory schemes (pp. 12-13), not defined in the text, taken as simple non-learned baselines.
metrics: Average content downloading delay (s); cumulative reward and convergence episodes; drone trajectory plot (pp. 10-13).
complexity: O(sum of n_l * n_(l+1)) over layers, approximated as O(n_l^2), for the DC-PPO neural network (p. 9); no FLOPs or runtime reported.
q1_support: p. 5: "a probabilistic line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS)" path-loss model from [33], [34] (Eqs. 8-13) in a custom simulator; no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing dataset or measured data.
q2_support: p. 3: "number of users, and number of content repository files on" the delay is compared; the paper never states that a model trained in one setting is tested in another, nor whether the agent is retrained per setting.
q3_support: p. 9: "Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm:" (also PPO, A2C); p. 12: "Obviously, our scheme significantly outperforms the other three" algorithms in delay; p. 12: "(ii) the random caching scheme, and (iii) the fixed trajectory" scheme, simple random and fixed baselines.
q4_support: p. 9: "the computational complexity can be approximated as" O(n_l^2) for the DC-PPO network, from O(sum of n_l n_(l+1)) over L fully connected layers; no FLOPs or runtime is given.
q5_support: p. 9: "a simulation platform was developed using Python 3.7.0" and Pytorch; the channel is simulated, with no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Included: the drone agent learns transmit power (physical layer, aerial link) jointly with caching placement and trajectory (above PHY), so the above_phy check passes (p. 6, action space). Area 6: aerial BS with learned power control; single-antenna links are admitted for NTN. q1: the LoS/NLoS air-to-ground model of [33], [34] is a literature path-loss model, not a standardized one, so counted as custom; reviewer may overrule. q3: PPO is the base of DC-PPO and is not counted; A2C and DDPG are the learned baselines; random caching and fixed trajectory are undefined in the text and taken as simple non-learned baselines, reviewer to confirm.
